vSNP3 GUI · step-by-step training (SOP)

Find where two outbreaks came from

You will install the vSNP3 web tool, download 26 real samples, run them, and read the answer from a tree. Every step shows what to do and what you should see.

TIME

About 3 hours the first time. Most of it is waiting while the computer downloads and works. Slow internet makes it longer.

YOU NEED

A Mac, Linux or Windows computer, internet, and about 50 GB of free disk space.

TESTED

1 October 2026, vSNP GUI v0.4.127, vsnp3 3.36. Newer versions may look a little different.

To move: click Next → at the bottom, or press the → arrow key.

vSNP3 GUI training · Kapur Lab · Penn State

Workflow/Step 1 and Step 2

The vSNP3 workflow.

Step 1 runs once per sample and fills a database that only grows. Step 2 works from the VCF files those alignments produced: defining SNPs make the groups, and each group is read as a tree and a SNP table.

vSNP3 GUI training · Kapur Lab · Penn State

The story

Our “database”: samples from Michigan and Texas

Bovine tuberculosis (Mycobacterium bovis) was found in two states.

21 samples came from known places: 7 from Michigan and 14 from Texas. Each one has a county name.

In this training, these 21 samples are our database: samples we already know.

Fake namesThe DNA data is real and public. The places, counties and outbreaks are made up for training. Every name ends in _notReal.

vSNP3 GUI training · Kapur Lab · Penn State

The story

Then two outbreaks start. Where did they come from?

OUTBREAK1: 3 new samples from Wisconsin.

OUTBREAK2: 2 new samples from New Mexico.

We do not know where these 5 samples came from. They are our unknowns.

Your mission: compare the 5 unknowns with the 21 database samples. Which county is each outbreak closest to?

HowvSNP3 finds the small DNA differences (SNPs) between samples. Few differences = closely related.

In real lifeThis training's database has known samples from only two states, Michigan and Texas. A real database would hold many more: every dot on the map is a past outbreak, and its samples could be in the database too.

The story

The plan

Four parts: A, B, C and D. Part C has four stages. The times are for a normal laptop.

  1. AInstall

    45–90 minutes

    Only the first time. You copy a few terminal commands from this guide.

  2. BStart here next time

    5 min

    How to open, check and update the tools on another day. Keep these pages.

  3. CRun the analysis

    1–2 hours

    In the vSNP3 web page, in four stages:

    1. C1–C5
      Get the data. Make a project and download the 26 samples.10–30 min
    2. C6–C10
      Step 1: align. Line up each sample on the reference genome and check its quality.20–60 min
    3. C11–C14
      Step 2: compare. Add the sample names, then compare all 26 samples.5 min
    4. C15–C20
      Read the answer. Find the red samples in the tree and count the SNPs.15 min
  4. DFinish

    5 min

    Check yourself, fix problems, and stop for today.

Already installed?Go to Part B: Start here next time.

Slow internet?The times are for good internet. Parts A and C download several GB. On a slow connection they can take two or three times longer.

Install (first time only)

A. Install (first time only)

A1 · What you need

Check this list before you start.

  • A Mac with macOS 13 or newer (Apple chip or Intel chip).
  • Your Mac password. You need it once, to install Apple's command-line tools.
  • About 50 GB of free disk space, and a good internet connection.
  • A Linux computer, for example Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04, with an Intel or AMD processor (some tools do not run on ARM).
  • Your password, for the sudo command (installing git).
  • About 50 GB of free disk space, and a good internet connection.
  • Windows 10 (version 22H2) or Windows 11, on a PC with an Intel or AMD processor (some tools do not run on Windows on ARM).
  • An administrator account. You use it once, to turn on WSL (Linux inside Windows).
  • About 50 GB of free disk space, and a good internet connection.
  • The tools run inside Ubuntu (Linux). You open the vSNP3 page in your normal Windows browser.

TimeAbout 45–90 minutes with good internet. Most of it is downloading: about 7 GB. On slow internet it takes longer, sometimes two or three times as long. That is normal: plan extra time, and keep the computer plugged in and awake.

Wrong computer?Look at My computer at the bottom of the screen. Click your type of computer.

A. Install (first time only)

A2 · Turn on Linux for Windows (WSL) Windows

Windows runs the tools inside Ubuntu, a version of Linux. You do this once.

▶ Do this

  1. Click Start. Type PowerShell.
  2. Right-click Windows PowerShell. Click Run as administrator. Click Yes.
  3. Copy this command, paste it in the blue window, and press Enter:
    wsl --install
  4. When it says the changes need a restart, restart the computer.

✔ You should see

After the restart, an Ubuntu window opens by itself. It asks you to make a user name and a password.

  • Type a short user name (small letters, no spaces). Press Enter.
  • Type a password. Press Enter. Type it again.
Ubuntu
Enter new UNIX username: 
ana
New password:
Installation successful!
ana@MY-PC:~$

RememberYou do not see the password while you type it. This is normal. Write the password down: you need it in the next step.

Next timeOpen Ubuntu from the Start menu: click Start, type Ubuntu, press Enter. In this guide, “terminal” means this Ubuntu window.

A. Install (first time only)

A3 · Get git and Rosetta 2 macOS

git downloads the tools for you. On a Mac it comes with Apple's free command-line tools.

▶ Do this

  1. Copy this command. Paste it in Terminal. Press Return.
    xcode-select --install
  2. A window asks to install the command line developer tools. Click Install, then Agree.
  3. Wait until it says the software was installed (5–15 minutes, longer on slow internet). Click Done.
  4. Check it:
    git --version
  5. Apple chip only (M1, M2, M3, M4 …): install Rosetta 2. If it asks for your password, type it and press Return.
    softwareupdate --install-rosetta --agree-to-license

✔ You should see

Step 4 shows a version number:

Terminal
$ git --version
git version 2.39.5 (Apple Git-154)

Any number is fine. After step 5, the prompt (%) comes back.

Which chip?Click the Apple menu (the apple at the top left of the screen), then About This Mac. Chip: Apple M… = Apple chip: do step 5. Processor: Intel = Intel chip: skip step 5.

Why Rosetta 2?Some programs that the tools use are made only for Intel chips. Rosetta 2 is Apple's free helper that runs them on an Apple chip.

Already installed?If Terminal says command line tools are already installed, that is good. Go on to step 4.

git downloads the tools for you. curl downloads files.

▶ Do this

A version number:

Not Ubuntu?On Fedora use sudo dnf install -y git curl. Many computers already have git.

vSNP3 GUI training · Kapur Lab · Penn State

A. Install (first time only)

A4 · Download Miniforge

The same command works on every computer. It picks the right file for you.

▶ Do this

  1. Go to your home folder:
    cd ~
  2. Download Miniforge (one long line; copy it with the button):
    curl -L -O "https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge/releases/latest/download/Miniforge3-$(uname)-$(uname -m).sh"

✔ You should see

A progress table. It ends with 100 on the left. Then the prompt comes back. The file is about 125 MB: seconds on fast internet, a few minutes on slow internet.

Terminal
$ curl -L -O "https://github.com/conda-forge/…/Miniforge3-$(uname)-$(uname -m).sh"
  % Total    % Received % Xferd  Average Speed   Time
100  118M  100  118M    0     0  93.6M      0  0:00:01
$

What is Miniforge?A free installer for conda. Conda installs vSNP3 and all the programs it needs, in their own folder. It does not change other programs on your computer.

Is it safe?Yes. Miniforge is free, open-source software from conda-forge, a large community project that scientists all over the world use every day. The command downloads it straight from conda-forge's official page on GitHub (github.com, a website owned by Microsoft). This training's tools come from GitHub too.

A5 · Run the Miniforge installer

Copy the command, paste it, press Enter.

The installer asks 5 questions. Answer them like this:

When you seeDo this

License text, and --More-- at the bottomPress Space until the next question comes
Do you accept the license terms? [yes|no]Type yes and press Enter
Press ENTER to confirm the locationPress Enter
Proceed with initialization? [yes|no]  [no] >>>Type yes and press Enter

ImportantThe last question says [no]. Do not just press Enter. Type yes.

installation finished.

A. Install (first time only)

A6 · Close the terminal and open a new one

Do not skip this step. The new window knows about conda. The old one does not.

▶ Do this

  1. Quit Terminal: press ⌘ Command + Q. Then open Terminal again (step A2).Close the terminal window. Open a new one (step A2).Close the Ubuntu window. Open Ubuntu again from the Start menu.
  2. Check conda:
    conda --version

✔ You should see

The prompt now starts with (base), and conda shows its version:

Terminal
(base) $ conda --version
conda 26.7.2

A newer number is fine.

Why this mattersThe installer has just changed your terminal's start-up settings, so that the terminal can find conda. A terminal that is already open still uses the old settings: only a new terminal reads the new ones. If you skip this step, the next steps fail with “conda: command not found”.

If it says “conda: command not found”You answered no to the last question in A5. Run this, then do A6 again: ~/miniforge3/bin/conda init

bdtoolsbdtools is the control program for these tools. It installs them, checks them, updates them and opens them.

Slow internet?This step downloads about 7 GB. One tool, kSNP, fetches a large package (520 MB, or about 1 GB on a Mac) from SourceForge, which is often slow: in our test that part alone took 19 minutes. On slow internet the whole step can take an hour or more. That is normal.

Why N?vSNP3 already has the reference genome we need. y downloads more than 50 GB of databases for other tools. You can add them later with bin/bdtools setup-databases.

✗ for two tools? That is expectedAMRFinderPlus and Kraken ID-Parse need extra databases, so the last lines say 2 tool(s) need attention. This training uses only vSNP3, so you can leave them. To set them up later: bin/bdtools setup-databases amrfinder (small), or bin/bdtools setup-databases kraken blast (very large). Lines that start with – are only notes.

B2 · The dashboard: check, update, restart, stop

Once the dashboard is open, its page does the rest. Keep this page.

I want to…On the dashboard pageOr in the terminal
Check that the tools are readyLook at the cards. A ready tool shows only its version. A tool with a problem says needs setup and lists the fix.bin/bdtools doctor

Your filesYour projects are in the projects folder in your home folder. Shut down and updates do not delete them.

B. Start here next time

B3 · Update the tools

New versions fix problems. The dashboard tells you when there is one.

▶ Do this

On the dashboard, scroll to the bottom. ✓ Up to date means there is nothing to do.

  1. If it says ↑ Updates available, click the button with the number 1 (here 1 Update bdtools). A box asks if you are sure: click OK.
  2. Wait until the log says Update finished and ✅ Finished. Then click ↻ Restart dashboard and OK.
  3. The box checks again. If a button is left (here 1 Install tool updates (1)), click it and OK. It rebuilds the tool: a few minutes.
  4. When it says ✅ Finished, click ↻ Restart dashboard again. Then click Launch on the vSNP3 card.

✔ You should see

Each update ends with Update finished and ✅ Finished under its log. After the last restart, the box says ✓ Up to date and the vSNP3 card shows the new version number. An old vSNP3 tab now says vsnp_gui is not running — launch it from the dashboard: close it and click Launch.

Slow internet?An update downloads new files, and may rebuild a tool. It takes a few minutes, longer on slow internet. Do not close the terminal while it runs.

In the terminalThe same, typed in the tools folder: git pull, then bin/bdtools update all, then bin/bdtools dashboard --restart. Updates keep your projects.

C. Run the analysis

C2 · Create a project

A project is a folder that keeps one analysis together.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs → Projects › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

Scroll down to Projects.

  1. Click the box New project name (e.g. LSDV_India) and type Outbreak_training.
  2. In the list -- reference (optional) --, choose Mycobacterium_AF2122.
  3. Click Create.

✔ You should see

A new card: Outbreak_training, with a green tag Mycobacterium_AF2122 and FASTQ: 0 | Step1: 0 | VCF DB: 0.

Why this reference?A reference is a known, complete genome. Mycobacterium_AF2122 is the standard M. bovis genome. Our samples are M. bovis.

C. Run the analysis

C4 · Download the 26 samples

vSNP3 downloads the DNA reads for you.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs → Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

First copy the 26 SRA numbers:

  1. In SRA Download, click the box SRR/SRX/SRS accessions (one per line) and paste.
  2. Leave Optional subfolder empty. Click Download.

✔ You should see

Under the button: Downloading 26 accessions… and a timer.

Where from?vSNP3 downloads the reads from a free public library (NCBI SRA, through the European copy at ENA). It downloads about 5 GB, so on slow internet this step takes a long time (see C5).

vSNP3 GUI training · Kapur Lab · Penn State

C. Run the analysis

C5 · Wait for the download

Each sample has two files: R1 and R2 (the two ends of each DNA piece).

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs → Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. Wait. Do not close the tab or the terminal.
  2. You can follow the progress in Live Logs at the bottom of the page.

✔ You should see

Download complete and Last download: 26 downloaded. On the right, Ready to run (26 samples) lists every sample as paired · R1+R2.

TimeAbout 10–30 minutes with good internet (5.1 GB). On slow internet it can take 1–2 hours. Our test took 16 minutes.

If some failedSometimes the download server refuses a file. Then the box says Failed — 1 and names the sample. Copy all 26 again, paste them, and click Download again. Samples you already have are skipped, so only the missing ones download.

C6 · Step 1: grab the samples

Step 1 needs the reads in its own folder. One button does it.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

Scroll down to Step 1. Reference already says Mycobacterium_AF2122.

  1. Do not tick any boxes. Click Grab ready-to-run samples.

✔ You should see

52 file(s) staged. The Samples list shows 26 samples, each Not Started.

Why 52?26 samples × 2 files (R1 and R2) = 52 files.

C7 · Step 1: run

This is the slow part. You can take a break.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 › Step 2 › Live Logs

▶ Do this

  1. Click Run (under Grab ready-to-run samples).

✔ You should see

The button says Running… with a timer, and a Stop button appears. Samples change from Not Started to Running to Complete. Three run at the same time.

TimeAbout 20–60 minutes on a laptop. Our test computer (a 64-core workstation) took 6 minutes.

What happensFor each sample, vSNP3 lines up millions of short reads on the reference genome and lists every place where the sample is different (a VCF file).

  2. Scroll the Samples list to check them all.

C9 · Check the quality

Before Step 2, check that every sample is good enough.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 → Step 1 Results › Step 2 › Live Logs

✔ You should see

Step 1 Results fills in by itself: Loaded 26 sample(s). 25 PASS and 1 REVIEW: SRR33585214, “mapping rate 89.8%”.

▶ Do this

  1. Scroll the table to the right to see Avg Depth and Mapping %. Check them with the table below.
  2. Do not tick Exclude. We keep all 26 samples.
ColumnGoodOursMeaning
Avg Depth20 or more38 to 116How many reads cover each letter of the genome, on average.
Mapping %90% or more90% to 100% (one 89.8%)How many reads match the reference.
Genome Covnear 100%about 99.5%How much of the genome has reads.

Why keep SRR33585214?Its mapping rate is just under 90%, so vSNP3 asks you to look. Its depth (38) is good, so the SNP calls are still reliable.

On the vSNP3 page: Settings › Projects & Inputs › Reference Editor › Step 1 → Step 1 Results › Step 2 › Live Logs

Look at the Groups column. vSNP3 already sorted every sample into a group, using a few defining SNPs:

  • The Michigan samples and the New Mexico samples are in Mbovis-04B6.
  • The Texas samples and the Wisconsin samples are in Mbovis-04C7.

ExampleIn the picture, SRR33629183 is a New Mexico sample (red, unknown). Its group is Mbovis-04B6, the same as the Michigan samples SRR33561021 and SRR33665434.

C17 · Read the tree

Look at the black name that joins each red group.

Where: the Tree viewer tab (it opened in C15). The vSNP3 page stays open in its own tab.

  • Samples that join with short lines have few SNPs between them. They are closely related.
  • The 3 Wisconsin samples join with SRR33914654 … TEXAS_countyF.

Where: the Tree viewer tab (it opened in C15). The vSNP3 page stays open in its own tab.

hiding 53 of 57 positions. Only 4 columns are left. Each coloured box is a difference.

Where: the Tree viewer tab (it opened in C15). The vSNP3 page stays open in its own tab.

C. Run the analysis

C20 · The answer

You found it. Here is what vSNP3 shows.

OUTBREAK1 · Wisconsin

is closest to

Texas · countyF

2–3 SNPs from sample SRR33914654 (2022). The next closest, Texas countyG, is 9–10 SNPs away.

OUTBREAK2 · New Mexico

is closest to

Michigan · countyX

2 SNPs from sample SRR33818626 (2021). Every other Michigan sample is 11 or more SNPs away.

How close is close?For TB, samples within about 5–12 SNPs may be part of the same chain of infection. The tree and the SNP table are two views of the same answer. Always look at both.

RememberThe places and outbreaks in this exercise are made up. The method is real.

D. Finish

D1 · Check yourself

Click a question to see the answer.

1. Why did we choose the reference Mycobacterium_AF2122?

Our samples are M. bovis. AF2122 is a complete M. bovis genome, so the reads match it well.

2. What does Step 1 make for each sample?

A VCF file: the list of places where the sample is different from the reference.

3. One sample said REVIEW. Why did we keep it?

Its mapping rate (89.8%) was just under 90%, but its depth (38) was good. The SNP calls are still reliable.

4. What does a short line between two samples in the tree mean?

Few SNPs between them. They are closely related.

5. Which county is OUTBREAK2 (New Mexico) closest to?

Michigan countyX, 2 SNPs away.

vSNP3 GUI training · Kapur Lab · Penn State

D. Finish

D2 · If something goes wrong

Most problems have a simple fix.

ProblemFix
conda: command not foundClose the terminal and open a new one (A6). Still there? Run ~/miniforge3/bin/conda init, then open a new terminal.
bin/bdtools: No such file or directoryYou are in the wrong folder. Run cd ~/bioinformatic_diagnostic_tools first.
The browser says it can't connect to 127.0.0.1:8080The dashboard is not running. Start it (B1). Keep the terminal open.
Buttons are pale and do nothingNo project is open. Click the project card (C3).
The download says Failed for some samplesPaste all 26 again and click Download. Only the missing samples download.
A sample in Step 1 says ErrorClick View log next to it to see why. To try again, tick Force re-run and click Run. (This runs all 26 samples again, so it takes the same time as the first run.)
The tree shows only SRR numbersThe names were not added before Step 2. Do C11, then run Step 2 again (C13).
Anything elseLook at the dashboard: a card that says needs setup lists the fix. Or, in the tools folder, run bin/bdtools doctor: it lists what is wrong and the command that fixes it.
